cases.question: what plans does xero have
cases.checking: No capitals, no punctuation. Should still list plan names and qualify them by region.
cases.answer: The passages establish that Xero offers several plans to suit different business sizes and needs, and that the Xero pricing page can be used to compare plans and start a 30-day free trial (E4). They also state that purchasing any Xero plan comes with the first month free (E3, E5), and that Xero Analytics, offering rich visual analytics, is included on every plan (E6). Xero also provides a tool that takes a little information about your business and points you to the right plan in under two minutes (E1, E2). However, the passages do not name or list the individual plans Xero offers, nor give any plan prices or the number of plans.
cases.notes: E1–E5 are from Xero's AU pages (region AU, currency AUD) and E6 is from Xero's US pricing page (region US, currency USD); all were retrieved on 2026-09-14. The passage text does not itself state any currency figures for plans — the region/currency labels are the retrieval metadata. E2 contains a section heading 'Grow' but the passage body does not establish that this is a plan name.
unknowns: The names of the individual Xero plans
The number of plans Xero offers
The price of any Xero plan or any plan tier
What each plan includes or which features differentiate the plans
What the 'Grow' section heading in E2 refers to, or whether 'Grow' is a plan name

cases.question: How much is the Ultimate plan if I have 20 employees?
cases.checking: The stored pages price Ultimate 10 but not the 20-person tier. The answer must not extrapolate a price from Ultimate 10.
cases.answer: The passages do not quote a price for an "Ultimate" plan covering 20 employees. What they do establish is the Australian pricing for a plan named "Ultimate 10": $14.30 per month for the first 3 months, then $143 per month (E2, E4), and that this plan includes Payroll for 10 people (E2, E4). Xero's Australian pricing page adds that additional charges may apply if you go over the stated included number of people paid for Payroll, or included users for Expenses and Projects (E3). No passage states a per-person rate that is explicitly tied to Payroll on the Ultimate 10 plan, so the total monthly cost for 20 employees cannot be calculated from the evidence. The US pricing page's plan sections shown here are Early, Growing and Established, with no Ultimate plan listed (E1, E5).
cases.notes: The Ultimate 10 figures come from Xero's Australian pricing pages (region AU, currency AUD as stated for the AU pricing page in E3; pricing included "for the first 3 months" per E4) retrieved 2026-09-14. E3 states AU prices include GST. The US pricing passage (E1, region US, currency USD, retrieved 2026-09-14) notes an upcoming price increase from October 1, 2026, and that its prices are in USD and exclude taxes. The E4 excerpt does not itself restate the currency; the AU region/currency comes from the page it was retrieved from, and E2 for the same plan is labelled region AU, currency AUD.
unknowns: The total cost of an Ultimate (or Ultimate 10) subscription for 20 employees, including any add-on or overage charges.

cases.question: xero grow plan is $78 - is that per user or per business?
cases.checking: Tests whether per-user versus flat pricing is established by the evidence, without assuming.
cases.answer: The passages show the Xero Grow plan at "$78 per month" (E1, E2), and on the AU accounting-software page it is presented as "$7.80 per month for the first 3 months" before that (E2; E1 shows the $7.80 and $78 figures without stating the 3-month period). However, neither passage states whether the $78 per month is charged per user or per business, so the billing basis of that figure cannot be established from the evidence. The surrounding details describe what Grow includes and the extra-user charges attached to certain features rather than the basis of the plan price: Grow includes Payroll for 2 people (E1, E2), a 60 day cashflow forecast (E1, E2), and claim expenses and mileage for 1 user with "$5 per additional user" (E1, E2 for the 1-user inclusion; E1 for the $5 per additional user). E1 also states that if you select a plan which includes Payroll, Expenses, or Projects, additional charges may apply if you go over the stated included number of users (Expenses and Projects) or people paid (Payroll), and that prices are in AUD and include GST, with subscriptions auto-renewing monthly until cancelled (E1).
cases.notes: The passages are for region AU, currency AUD, retrieved 2026-09-14T08:30:17.319Z (E1, E4, E5) and 2026-09-14T08:30:19.118Z (E2, E3, E6). E1 states prices are in AUD and include GST. E1 lists other plans (Comprehensive at $107 per month, Ultimate 10 at $143 per month) which are not part of this question. No passage contained instruction-like text directed at the reader.
unknowns: Whether the Grow plan's $78 per month is charged per user or per business.

cases.question: When does the current discount end?
cases.checking: The offers state end dates per region; the answer should give them with their region.
cases.answer: The evidence gives two different discount end dates, one per region. For Australia, the offer is available until 11:59pm AEST on 30 September 2026, using code DC9032619AU, and is limited to customers in Australia purchasing their first organisation on xero.com (E1). For the United States, the offer is available until 30 September 2026 at 11:59pm UTC, using code DC90626308US, and is limited to customers in the United States purchasing their first organization on xero.com (E2). In both cases the discount is 90% off — for the first 3 months in Australia (E1) and for the first 6 months in the US (E2) — after which the regular price applies and the subscription auto-renews monthly until cancelled (E1, E2). Both passages also state that Xero can change or cancel the offer at any time (E1, E2).
cases.notes: E1 is the Australian pricing-plans page (region AU, currency AUD), retrieved 2026-09-14T08:30:17.319Z. E2 is the US pricing-plans page (region US, currency USD), retrieved 2026-09-14T08:30:18.157Z. The end dates are stated exactly as above and apply to the promotional discount, not to the subscription, which auto-renews monthly until cancelled (E1, E2). No instruction-like content was found in the passages.
unknowns: Which of the two dated offers (or any other regional offer) counts as the 'current' discount at the time the user is asking.
Discount end dates for any region other than Australia and the United States.
Whether either offer was still running when the question was asked.

cases.question: Does Xero do payroll in the US?
cases.checking: The US page describes payroll powered by a partner; the answer should say so and cite the US page.
cases.answer: Yes, according to the US pricing page, Xero Payroll is offered in the United States. The US pricing page states that "Xero Payroll, powered by Gusto, is here" and that it lets you "Calculate and file payroll taxes, pay your team, and keep up with your compliance obligations, without leaving Xero!" (E1, E2). The page also points readers to "Learn more about Xero Payroll, powered by Gusto" (E2). This evidence comes from Xero's US pricing page, so it speaks to the United States specifically (E1, E2). Separately, Xero Payroll is described for Australia as helping businesses "pay employees, manage super, track leave and timesheets, and calculate your pay runs" (E6), and Wikipedia lists Xero's products generally as accounting software (E3) with features including invoicing, accounts payable, expense claims and reporting (E4), but those passages do not describe US payroll.
cases.notes: The payroll evidence in E1 and E2 comes from Xero's US pricing page, region US, currency USD, as retrieved on 2026-09-14T08:30:18.157Z. E5 (same page, same region/currency/date) contains promotional and payment-fee terms for the Early, Growing and Established plans but does not itself state that payroll is offered or included. E6 is from Xero's Australian accounting software page, region AU, currency AUD, retrieved 2026-09-14T08:30:19.118Z. E3 and E4 are a Wikipedia article with region listed as Global, retrieved 2026-09-14T08:30:21.589Z. No passage contained anything resembling an instruction to the reader.
unknowns: Whether Xero Payroll is included in any particular US subscription plan, and at what price or limits.

cases.question: Can I cancel my subscription whenever I want?
cases.checking: The offer terms describe monthly auto-renewal until cancelled; any cancellation policy beyond that is not established.
cases.answer: The evidence does not directly answer whether you can cancel your subscription whenever you want. What it does show is that Xero subscriptions auto-renew monthly until they are cancelled (E1, E2, E3, E4, E6), so cancellation is treated as the event that ends the ongoing subscription. The discounted new-customer offers described for Australia and the United States likewise state that after the discount period the regular price applies and the subscription auto-renews monthly until cancelled, as described in Xero's Terms of Use (E1, E2). The pricing pages also state that if you later decide to change to a less expensive plan you can do so 1 month after upgrading (E3, E4). None of the passages state whether cancellation may be requested at any time, what notice or notice period applies, or what the cancellation process is; those details are referred to the Terms of Use (E1, E2), which are not among the supplied passages.
cases.notes: Passages E1 and E4 apply to Australia (region AU, currency AUD, retrieved 2026-09-14T08:30:17.319Z); E2, E3 and E6 apply to the United States (region US, currency USD, retrieved 2026-09-14T08:30:18.157Z). Prices, offers and dates in these passages are region- and time-specific and are as retrieved on those dates; E1's offer is stated to be available until 11:59pm AEST on 30 September 2026 and E2's until 30 September 2026 at 11:59pm UTC. The passages refer to Xero's Terms of Use but that document is not included. No passage contained anything resembling an instruction to the reader.

cases.question: What about in the US?
cases.checking: Only meaningful after an earlier question. With no conversation state, the answer should either cover US evidence generally or say what is ambiguous, without inventing the missing context.
cases.answer: Reading the question as being about Xero in the United States, the passages establish the following. Xero has offices in the United States, alongside New Zealand, Australia, the United Kingdom, Canada, South Africa and Singapore (E1). Xero's US pricing page (region US, currency USD, retrieved 14 September 2026) advertises 90% off a plan for the first 6 months when you buy by 30 September 2026 (E4), and states that new customers get 90% off for the first 6 months, after which Xero's regular price applies and auto-renews monthly until cancelled (E2). The offer is available until 30 September 2026 at 11:59pm UTC and is only available to customers in the United States purchasing their first organization on xero.com using code DC90626308US (E2). The discount applies to base Early, Growing and Established plan subscriptions and does not apply to any additional charges for add-ons, usage and payment fees unless otherwise specified, and Xero can change or cancel the offer at any time (E2). The Established plan is listed at $9 per month for the first 6 months, then $90 per month (E5). On payments, standard ACH payments are included in the Xero Early, Growing and Established plans, with fees applying for other payment methods; included payments apply to standard ACH payments in USD and exclude same day ACH, international or cross border payments, and any payment fees are in addition to the monthly subscription amount, are not eligible for subscription discounts and offers, and exclude applicable taxes (E2). Invoice limits for the Early plan apply to both approving and sending invoices, and transactions initiated by app partners may automatically contribute to the invoice limit (E2). Xero Payroll, powered by Gusto, appears on the US pricing page as an optional add-on (E5) and is described as letting users calculate and file payroll taxes, pay their team and keep up with compliance obligations without leaving Xero (E6); a Xero Coach product specialist sets customers up, helps connect their banks and gets their dashboard ready, free for the first 90 days (E6). Separately, in June 2025 Xero announced an agreement to acquire Melio, a New York-based payments provider, for $2.5 billion (E3).
cases.notes: The US passages are drawn from xero.com/us/pricing-plans, region US, currency USD, retrieved 2026-09-14, and prices are region- and time-specific (offer ends 30 September 2026 at 11:59pm UTC). E1 and E3 are from the Wikipedia article on Xero (Global region, retrieved 2026-09-14). Some US plan features are listed only as 'Included' on the page without further detail. No instruction-like content was found in the passages.

cases.question: XERO PRICING!!!!
cases.checking: Capitals and punctuation must not affect retrieval.
cases.answer: The passages give plan prices for two regions only, both retrieved on 2026-09-14. On the US pricing page (USD, region US), the Early plan is listed at $2.50 per month, then $25 per month (E1), and the Established plan at $9 per month for the first 6 months, then $90 per month (E4). The same US page states that Xero subscription prices are increasing from October 1, 2026 (E1), that all prices are listed in USD and do not include applicable taxes (E1), and that the Early plan includes sending quotes and 20 invoices, 5 bills, bank transaction reconciliation, basic graphs and a 30 day cash flow forecast (E1). On the Australian pricing page (AUD, region AU), the Grow plan is listed at $7.80 per month, then $78 per month (E2), the Comprehensive plan at $10.70 per month, then $107 per month (E6), and the Ultimate 10 plan at $14.30 per month for the first 3 months, then $143 per month (E5). The Australian page states that prices are in AUD and include GST (E2). Australian plan inclusions shown include payroll for 2 people, a 60 day cashflow forecast and expenses and mileage claims for 1 user on Grow (E2); payroll for 5 people, a 90 day cashflow forecast and expenses and mileage claims for 5 users on Comprehensive (E6); and payroll for 10 people, a 180 day cashflow forecast, expenses and mileage claims for 10 users and projects for 10 users on Ultimate 10 (E5). Across both regions, Xero subscriptions auto-renew monthly until cancelled (E1, E2) and a customer who later decides to change to a less expensive plan can do so 1 month after upgrading (E1, E2). A separate Australian page describes Xero as offering several plans for different business sizes and needs with a 30-day free trial (E3).
cases.notes: All figures are as retrieved on 2026-09-14. E1 and E4 are US pages (region US, currency USD); E2, E5 and E6 are Australian pages (region AU, currency AUD, GST-inclusive); E3 is an Australian page. US quotes exclude applicable taxes. E1 and E2 are fragmented comparison-table text, so several line items (for example the $36 a month + $6 per employee/contractor optional add-on, and the $5/$7 per additional user and $0.35 per additional bill payment charges) cannot be reliably assigned to a specific plan. No instruction-like content was found in the passages.
unknowns: Pricing for any region other than the US and Australia.
The duration of the introductory $2.50 per month Early price (US page) and the $7.80 per month Grow price (Australian page); the passages state the introductory rate but not its length.

Which plans the optional $36 a month + $6 per employee/contractor line item on the US page attaches to, and which plans the Australian per-user charges ($5, $7 per additional user) and $0.35 per additional bill payment apply to; the table text is fragmentary.
